posts.title: They Met With Us. Then Made It Worse.
posts.excerpt: We met with Council Members Pete Festersen and Danny Begley. They said they would try to include affordable housing, food access, and business relocation support in the TIF agreement. None of it appeared. Instead they added a provision preventing renters from contesting property tax increases.
posts.author: Saddle Creek Merchants United + Grammercy Park Collective

videos.label: Omaha City Council meeting — Pete Festersen commits on record to community engagement requirements, February 2026
KETV: City Council advances project despite TIF and affordable housing concerns, February 4, 2026

posts.body:
## Watch: Festersen on record

The February 4, 2026 KETV report and the city council meeting recording are embedded above. In the council meeting, Festersen stated on the record that he would require the developer to engage with the community. Watch what he said, then read what happened.

## What They Said

Representatives from our coalition met with Council Members Pete Festersen and Danny Begley ahead of the Saddle Creek Marketplace TIF and EEA votes. We raised specific concerns and received specific responses. They told us they would try to include:

- Affordable housing units in the development
- A food access requirement, given Family Fare's departure from a neighborhood already facing food access challenges
- Support for the businesses being displaced, including relocation assistance

We left that meeting cautiously hopeful. We should not have been.

## What They Did

None of those commitments appeared in the final TIF agreement.

Instead, a provision was added preventing renters in the affected area from contesting property tax increases. In a neighborhood where renters are already under pressure, this is not a neutral technical detail. It is a protection stripped from the people most vulnerable to displacement, written into a public subsidy agreement for a luxury apartment developer.

Begley and Festersen bent to the developer. They did not deliver what they promised our community.

## The Numbers

The developer, Mitch Hohlen of Woodsonia, is seeking $9 million in Tax Increment Financing and $12 million in Enhanced Employment Area designation, an occupation tax, for a total of $21 million in public subsidy on a $110 million project. There is no affordable housing. There is no food access guarantee. There is no relocation support for the seven businesses being demolished.

## What We Are Asking

We are asking every council member to vote NO on June 2. We are asking the mayor's office to intervene. And we are asking our neighbors, our community, and anyone who cares about how public money is spent in Omaha to show up or email before the final hearing.

Saddle Creek runs deep. We will not pay for our own displacement.

posts.title: WOWT: Neighbors Question $21M in Public Funding for Luxury Apartments
posts.excerpt: WOWT investigates the $110 million Saddle Creek Marketplace proposal: 223 luxury apartments, $21 million in public TIF and EEA funding, no affordable housing, and a grocery gap that would leave the nearest store two miles away with no bus service.
posts.author: WOWT 6 News
posts.body:
## Coverage from WOWT 6 News

WOWT's First Alert 6 Investigations team reported on the Saddle Creek Marketplace proposal in January 2026, raising questions neighbors have been asking since the project was announced.

The development would replace the Midtown Plaza shopping center at 46th and Cuming with 223 luxury apartments and 67,000 square feet of retail space. Developer Mitch Hohlen is seeking $9 million in Tax Increment Financing and $12 million in Enhanced Employment Area designation, a total of $21 million in public subsidy. The total project cost is $110 million. There is no affordable housing in the proposal.

Hohlen previously built The Artisan at 39th, also TIF-funded. Studios there start at $1,150 per month. Two-bedrooms run up to $2,470. The Saddle Creek Marketplace is described as similar.

### No affordable housing

Neighbor Josh Livingston told WOWT: at the first meeting, conversations about affordable housing were met with a clear indication that was not part of the plan.

### The grocery gap

Family Fare's departure from Midtown Plaza would leave the nearest grocery store two miles away, with no direct bus service. Residents want assurance that food access will be addressed before any public money is committed.

### Watch KETV's coverage

KETV also reported on the project. Watch their coverage and read the full story at the links below.

**Read:** [WOWT — Neighbors question public funding for luxury apartments](https://www.wowt.com/2026/01/29/neighbors-question-9m-public-funding-luxury-apartments-dundee-redevelopment/)

**Watch:** [KETV — $103 million development project near Saddle Creek Road](https://www.facebook.com/ketv7/videos/a-103-million-development-project-near-saddle-creek-road-and-northeast-of-46th-a/1565167058071517/)

posts.title: Coalition Statement: End the N. Saddle Creek BID
posts.excerpt: Saddle Creek Merchants United and Grammercy Park Collective are calling for the dissolution of the N. Saddle Creek Business Improvement District. Here is why, and what we want instead.
posts.author: Saddle Creek Merchants United + Grammercy Park Collective
posts.body:
## Our Position

Saddle Creek Merchants United and Grammercy Park Collective are calling for the dissolution of the N. Saddle Creek Business Improvement District.

A well-governed business improvement district can be a genuinely useful community institution. The N. Saddle Creek BID is not that. It has never been that.

## What the BID Actually Is

The BID's leadership consists of a developer and his wife who live outside the neighborhood, his tenant, and one other absentee property owner. There is no meaningful local representation. The businesses required by law to fund it have no real voice in how it operates.

The BID meets at a storage facility two miles from Saddle Creek. It has never provided transparent public accounting of how assessment funds are spent. It has required mandatory funds to pay for private security to manage problems created by the developer's own neglected properties.

## The Road Closure

A public access road was closed at the developer's request, over the objections of businesses and residents. The developer is now attempting to replat and sell that public land as a private lot.

## What We Are Asking For

- Dissolution of the N. Saddle Creek BID in its current form
- A full independent audit of BID expenditures
- Reversal of the public road closure
- Any future business improvement district to be built from the ground up with authentic community governance

Contact us at saddlecreekbid@gmail.com.

posts.title: Two Projects, One Community: Why We Formed This Coalition
posts.excerpt: Saddle Creek Merchants United and Grammercy Park Collective are joining forces. Here is who we are and what we are fighting for.
posts.author: Saddle Creek Merchants United + Grammercy Park Collective
posts.body:
## Two Organizations, One Goal

Saddle Creek Merchants United represents the independent businesses of the N. Saddle Creek corridor. Many are family-owned, deeply rooted in this neighborhood, and required by law to fund a Business Improvement District that has never represented their interests.

Grammercy Park Collective is a community group that does a lot of things, including organizing events and bringing neighbors together. We are supporting this initiative because so many of our neighbors found themselves with no voice in decisions that directly affected their streets and their lives.

We are joining forces because the problems facing Saddle Creek affect everyone who lives and works here.

## What We Are Up Against

Two separate development projects closing in from both ends of the corridor. An unaccountable Business Improvement District controlled by outside developer interests. A $110 million luxury apartment proposal seeking $21 million in public TIF and EEA funding, with no affordable housing and no plan to replace the grocery access being lost when Family Fare closes.

Saddle Creek runs deep. We will not pay for our own displacement.

Email us at saddlecreekbid@gmail.com to get involved.
